working_title: Rainwater: Catch It, Store It, Use It

owner_input.owner_notes: Process strong spin-off opportunities through the normal Research gate. Preserve Water Through the Layers at Product Design/Visual work; do not reopen its approved research foundation unless a specific Product Design evidence gap is routed back.

context_review.learning_area_reason: Rainwater harvesting is directly about water, land, food/resource systems, homestead resilience and practical self-reliance. The system-thinking and budgeting lessons also transfer into Personal Capability and Money/Business learning areas.

conflicts_found: Rainwater is a legitimate water source and can be treated for potable use, but untreated rooftop rainwater is not automatically drinking-water safe. Catchment material, airborne/roof contamination, storage conditions and intended use materially change the treatment and verification burden.

First-flush diversion often improves quality, especially after dry periods, but no universal diversion volume is scientifically valid for every roof/climate; roof area, debris load, dry period, rainfall intensity and catchment material matter.

Different institutions take different default positions on household use. UF/IFAS frames ordinary homeowner rainwater systems as non-potable, while CDC/WHO and Bermuda evidence show rainwater can be part of drinking-water systems when collection, treatment, maintenance and verification are appropriate. RRA should teach the function/evidence boundary rather than flatten these into one rule.
